issues.issue: The proviso excluding instruments redeemable below purchase price says clause (B) does not apply to "units of money market funds pursuant to clause (v) above," but clause (v) is guaranteed reinvestment agreements and money market funds are clause (viii). The carve-out points at the wrong category of investment.

The subtraction in clause (ii) is "the sum of (a) the related Servicing Fee, (b) the Master Servicing Fee Rate and (c) the LPMI Fee," mixing a per annum rate into a sum of dollar amounts. The shortfall cannot be computed as written.

The definition ends with "or any replacement policy therefor through the related Interest Accrual Period for such Class relating to a Distribution Date," language that has no referent for "such Class" in a policy definition. Whether and for how long a replacement policy counts as a Primary Mortgage Insurance Policy is unintelligible.

Clause (d) counts the Stated Principal Balance of loans repurchased by "the Sponsor pursuant to Sections 2.02 or 2.03," omitting EMC, the other Seller obliged to repurchase under Section 2.02(c) and the definition of Seller. Principal recovered on an EMC repurchase falls outside Principal Funds.

This "Purchase Price" differs from the "Purchase Price" separately defined in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement, which nets Servicing Advances and Advances only where the purchaser is also the servicer and awards predatory-lending damages to the Purchaser rather than the Trust. Since repurchases are made under that agreement but the price is deposited under this one, the two definitions must be reconciled.

REMIC I is defined as "the segregated pool of assets described in the Preliminary Statement and Section 6.07(a)," the identical formula used for REMIC II, so the cross-reference does not distinguish the two pools. Which assets constitute REMIC I must be worked out from elsewhere.

A REMIC Opinion must say the action "will not have an adverse effect on any REMIC created hereunder," without specifying the kind of adverse effect (loss of REMIC status, a prohibited transactions tax, or any economic detriment). The trigger for delivering, and the sufficiency of, such an opinion is left vague.

Clause (ix) requires a Replacement Mortgage Loan to "comply with each representation and warranty set forth in Section 2.03 hereof," but Section 2.03 contains only Wells Fargo's corporate representations; the loan-level warranties are in Sections 8 and 10 of the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement. The substitution condition as drafted tests nothing about the replacement loan.

The Reserve Fund is said to be created "pursuant to Section 6.08 hereof," while Section 4.22(b) directs the Securities Administrator to establish the Reserve Fund on or before the Closing Date and Section 6.08 is the Class P Certificate Account. Which section governs the fund's creation and operation is contradictory.

The Saxon Assignment Agreement is said to be "attached hereto as Exhibit R-3," but Exhibit R-3 is the Wells Fargo Assignment, Assumption and Recognition Agreement per the exhibit list and the Wells Fargo Assignment Agreement definition. Two different agreements are assigned the same exhibit.

"Seller" is defined as EMC and the Sponsor, neither of which is a party to this Agreement under the preliminary paragraph, yet the Agreement imposes duties on "the Seller" (for example Section 4.20's financing-statement obligation and Section 4.02's direction right). Whether those obligations bind anyone under this instrument requires reading it against the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement.

The final sentence provides that "[n]o Servicer shall be required to make any Nonrecoverable Servicing Advances," a term the Agreement never defines; only "Nonrecoverable Advance" is defined and it addresses Advances, not Servicing Advances. The scope of the limitation is left to construction.

The single sentence runs "amounts received ... (net of expenses) or surplus amounts held ... to cover estimated expenses (including ... recoveries in respect of the representations and warranties made by the Seller pursuant to the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement) specifically related to a Mortgage Loan," so it is unclear whether repurchase-related recoveries are Subsequent Recoveries or merely an example of estimated expenses. The syntax determines whether rep-and-warranty recoveries reduce Realized Losses.

"Substitution Adjustment Amount" is given the meaning ascribed "pursuant to Section 2.03(d)," but Section 2.03 has only subsections (a) and (b) and the term is coined in an unlettered paragraph. The definitional cross-reference points to nothing.

The Tax Matters Person is "[t]he Holder of the greatest Percentage Interest" in the related class of Residual Certificates, with no tie-breaker if two holders hold equal interests and no mechanism for a change in holdings. The identity of the Tax Matters Person can therefore be indeterminate.

Prong (i)(A) measures the delinquency ratio against "31.55% of the Current Specified Enhancement Percentage" while prong (i)(B) uses "39.59%, of the Class M-1 Enhancement Percentage," and prong (ii) measures cumulative losses "as of the related Prepayment Period" rather than as of a date. Whether a Trigger Event exists turns on resolving these formulations.

Item (vi) includes in the Trust Fund "the rights under the Swap Administration Agreement relating to the Certificates," while the definition of Supplemental Interest Trust states that the Swap Administration Agreement, the Swap Agreement and the Swap Account "do not constitute parts of the Trust Fund." The two definitions cannot both be given effect as to those rights.

The allocation gives 93% to the Class A, M and B Certificates, 3% to the Class CE Certificates and 1% to each of the Class P, R-1, R-2, R-3 and RX Certificates, which totals 101% of the voting rights. Any vote requiring a specified percentage of Voting Rights cannot be computed as drafted.

The definition reads "the cap contract, dated Agreement Provider," omitting both the date and the counterparty to the Yield Maintenance Agreement. The instrument being incorporated is identified only by the Exhibit M-2 reference.

The recital says the Sellers conveyed "all the right, title and interest of the Sellers in and to the assets in the Mortgage Loans," a phrase that does not plainly convey the Mortgage Loans themselves as opposed to some subset of related assets. What passed from the Sellers to the Depositor is left to construction.

The Depositor conveys "the Trust Fund," but the Trust Fund definition includes the Special Deposit, which the last paragraph of Section 2.01 says is transferred by EMC, and rights under agreements to which the Depositor is not the counterparty. Whether those items passed under this granting clause requires reading it with the Trust Fund definition and Section 2.01's final paragraph.

The delivery obligation is imposed on the Depositor, yet the proviso permits "the Seller" to deliver substitute documents and the clause (x) certification is to be made by "the Seller or the title Servicer." Whose failure to deliver constitutes a document defect for purposes of Section 2.02 is left unclear.
